title: Nonpositivity of inner products under projection off a unit vector
statement:
Let $V$ be a real inner product space, let $u \in V$ be a unit vector, and let $x, y \in V$ satisfy $\langle x, u\rangle \le 0$, $\langle y, u\rangle \le 0$, and $\langle x, y\rangle \le 0$. Then the components of $x$ and $y$ orthogonal to $u$ again have nonpositive inner product:
\[
\langle\, x - \langle x, u\rangle\, u,\ y - \langle y, u\rangle\, u \,\rangle \le 0.
\]
hypotheses_covered: V is a real inner product space
replaced:
Let $V$ be a real inner product space, $u \in V$ a unit vector, and $x,y \in V$ with
$\langle x,u\rangle \le 0$, $\langle y,u\rangle \le 0$ and $\langle x,y\rangle \le 0$.
Then the components of $x$ and $y$ orthogonal to $u$ satisfy
$\langle x - \langle x,u\rangle u,\ y - \langle y,u\rangle u\rangle \le 0$.
